Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that this can be a really challenging and overwhelming time for new mothers, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any areas where you might need some extra support.

The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's commonly used in the postpartum context to make sure new mothers are getting the care they need. Please know that everything we discuss today is completely confidential, and I'm here to create a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings.

We'll be going through 10 questions together, and I'll be taking some notes to help me understand your responses. Don't worry, this is a judgment-free zone, and I'm here to listen and support you, not to criticize or diagnose. My goal is to get a better understanding of how you're feeling and to provide you with any resources or support that might be helpful to you right now.

So, let's get started. Can you tell me a little bit about how you've been feeling over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually enjoy, or have you been feeling overwhelmed or struggling to cope with your new role as a mother?

.. I've been feeling really tired, all the time. I mean, I know that's normal with a new baby, but it's hard to explain. I just feel like I'm running on empty, you know? And it's not just the lack of sleep, it's like my body and mind are just exhausted. Some days are better than others, but most days I feel like I'm just trying to keep my head above water.

As for enjoying things, it's been harder lately. I used to love reading and taking walks, but now it's hard to find the time or energy for those things. And even when I do get a chance to do something I enjoy, I don't always feel like I'm really enjoying it. It's like my mind is elsewhere, worrying about the baby or feeling guilty for taking a break. But at the same time, I do get happy moments with my baby, like when she smiles at me or falls asleep in my arms. Those moments make everything feel worth it, you know?

I've also been feeling a little anxious, especially at night when my baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe her. I worry that I'm not doing something right, or that she's not healthy. It's like my mind starts racing and I feel overwhelmed. But my husband has been really supportive, and he helps me calm down and reminds me that we're figuring this out together.

Overall, I guess I'd say that I'm coping, but some days are definitely harder than others. And I do feel like I'm struggling to adjust to this new role as a mother. It's just so much responsibility, and I want to make sure I'm doing everything right for my baby.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I'd say that's true for me, but not as much as it used to be. I mean, I still laugh and joke with my husband, and we have our moments where we look at each other and just laugh at the absurdity of it all, like when our baby does something silly or unexpected. But it's not as frequent as it was before having the baby. I feel like I've lost a bit of my sense of humor, and things that used to make me laugh just don't seem as funny anymore.

Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions, and I have to remind myself to appreciate the little things and find the humor in them. But when I do laugh, it feels really good, and it's like a weight has been lifted off my shoulders. My husband has been trying to make me laugh more, and it's helpful to have him around to remind me not to take things too seriously.

I think it's just hard for me to find the funny side of things when I'm feeling so tired and overwhelmed all the time. But I'm trying to make an effort to laugh more and not get too caught up in the stress of being a new mom.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, I haven't been looking forward to things as much as I used to. I mean, I'll plan something, like a walk with my husband or a visit with friends, and I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but I won't really feel excited about it until it's actually happening. And even then, sometimes I'll feel anxious or overwhelmed, and I'll think, "Oh no, I don't know if I can do this."

It's hard to explain, but it's like I've lost a bit of my enthusiasm for things. I used to love planning outings and trying new things, but now it all just feels like so much work. And with the baby, I always have to consider her needs and schedule, so it's hard to make plans without feeling stressed about it.

That being said, there are some things that I do look forward to, like my baby's bath time or reading her a bedtime story. Those moments are really special to me, and I feel happy and connected to her during those times. But overall, I'd say that I haven't been looking forward to things with the same level of enjoyment as I used to, and that's been a bit of a challenge for me.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... I'd say that's been happening to me a bit more often than I'd like to admit. As a new mom, I feel like I'm already questioning myself all the time, wondering if I'm doing everything right for my baby. And when things don't go as planned, it's easy for me to fall into the trap of thinking, "Oh, it's my fault. I should have done this or that differently."

Like, the other day, my baby was crying and I couldn't seem to soothe her, no matter what I tried. And I started thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I calm her down? Am I not doing something right?" It's like, I know it's not rational, but it's hard not to take it personally when things don't go well.

My husband tries to reassure me and tell me that it's not my fault, that it's just part of being a new mom, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of self-doubt. I feel like I'm already under so much pressure to be perfect, to be this amazing mom, and when things don't go right, it's easy to blame myself.

But, I guess, if I'm being honest, it's not all the time. Sometimes I can step back and think, "Okay, this is just one of those days," and I can try to be kinder to myself. But it's definitely something I struggle with, and I'm trying to work on being more gentle with myself and not beating myself up over every little thing.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... I'd say that's been happening to me quite a bit lately. As a new mom, I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something ridiculous, like "What if she chokes on something?" or "What if I'm not producing enough milk?" And it's not just during the day, either - at night, when the house is quiet and I'm lying in bed, my mind starts racing and I'll think about all the things that could go wrong.

It's like, I know it's irrational, but I just can't seem to shake off the feeling of anxiety. And it's not just about my baby, either - sometimes I'll worry about things that have nothing to do with her, like "What if I forget to pay a bill?" or "What if something happens to my husband?" It's like my brain is just constantly looking for things to worry about.

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, and he's been really supportive, but it's hard to explain to him how I'm feeling. He'll tell me, "Everything is fine, just relax," but it's not that easy. I feel like I'm always on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong.

Sometimes, when I'm feeling really anxious, I'll try to distract myself by doing something else, like taking a walk or reading a book. But even then, my mind will start wandering and I'll start worrying about something else. It's exhausting, to be honest. I just wish I could turn off my brain and relax, you know?
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... I'd say that's happened to me a few times, especially at night when everything is quiet and I'm alone with my thoughts. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or just watching her sleep, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. It's like, I know there's no reason to be scared, but I just can't shake off the feeling.

It's usually when I'm thinking about my baby's health or safety. I'll start worrying about things like SIDS or accidents, and before I know it, I'm in a full-blown panic. I'll think to myself, "What if something happens to her? What if I'm not doing enough to protect her?" And it's hard to calm myself down, because my mind just keeps racing with all these worst-case scenarios.

Sometimes, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll feel this overwhelming sense of fear. I'll be thinking, "What if I'm not a good enough mom? What if I'm messing everything up?" And it's hard to go back to sleep, because my mind is just racing with all these anxious thoughts.

My husband has been really helpful when this happens. He'll talk to me and calm me down, remind me that everything is okay and that we're doing our best as parents. But even with his support, it's hard to shake off the feeling of panic. It's like, I know it's irrational, but it's just so hard to control my thoughts and feelings sometimes.

It's funny, because during the day, I'm usually okay. I mean, I'll have my anxious moments, but I can usually distract myself with tasks and activities. But at night, when everything is quiet and I'm alone with my thoughts, that's when the panic and fear really start to creep in.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... I'd say that's been happening to me a lot lately. As a new mom, I feel like I'm constantly being pulled in a million different directions. I'm trying to take care of my baby, and my husband, and our home, and it's just feeling really overwhelming. Some days, I feel like I'm doing okay, like I'm managing to keep everything together. But other days, it feels like everything is just too much for me.

I'll be trying to do one thing, like making dinner or folding laundry, and my baby will start crying, and I'll have to drop everything to attend to her. And then, when I'm trying to soothe her, my husband will come to me with some problem or question, and I'll feel like I'm being pulled in two different directions. It's like, I know I'm not alone, and I have my husband's support, but sometimes it feels like I'm shouldering all of this responsibility on my own.

And it's not just the big things, either. It's the little things, too, like remembering to buy diapers or scheduling doctor's appointments. It's like, my brain is just constantly racing with all of these tasks and responsibilities, and it's hard to keep track of everything.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, feeling completely overwhelmed, and I'll just start crying. It's like, I don't know how much more I can handle, you know? But then, my husband will come and talk to me, and he'll remind me that we're in this together, and that we'll figure it out as a team. And that helps, a little bit.

But, yeah, I'd say that things have been getting on top of me a lot lately. It's just feeling really hard to manage everything, and to take care of myself, too. I feel like I'm running on empty, most of the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... I'd say that's been true for me, especially on some nights. I'll be lying in bed, trying to sleep, but my mind will be racing with thoughts and worries. I'll think about my baby, and whether she's okay, and whether I'm doing everything right for her. And then I'll start worrying about other things, like our finances, or our relationship, or just life in general.

It's hard to turn off my brain, you know? I'll be lying there, feeling anxious and overwhelmed, and I'll think to myself, "Why can't I just relax? Why can't I just sleep?" But my mind just won't shut off.

Some nights are worse than others, though. When I'm feeling really down or overwhelmed, it's like my brain is just wired to stay awake. I'll lie there for hours, staring at the ceiling, feeling like I'm the only one awake in the world. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll often wake up in the middle of the night, feeling anxious or scared.

It's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, either. It's the feeling of being exhausted all the time, but not being able to rest. I'll be so tired, but my mind will be racing, and I'll feel like I'm stuck in this constant state of alertness. It's like my body is screaming for rest, but my brain just won't cooperate.

My husband has been trying to help me with sleep, though. He'll take care of the baby at night, and let me get some rest. And sometimes, that helps. But other times, even with his help, I'll still lie awake, feeling anxious and overwhelmed. It's like, I know I need sleep, but my brain just won't let me have it.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... I'd say that's been true for me, especially on some days. As a new mom, I feel like I'm under so much pressure to be happy and excited all the time, but the truth is, some days are just really hard. I'll be feeling overwhelmed and exhausted, and I'll just feel sad. I'll think to myself, "Why can't I just be happy? Why can't I just enjoy this time with my baby?"

It's like, I know I'm supposed to be grateful for this little life that I've been given, and I am, but it's just hard sometimes. The lack of sleep, the constant worry, the feeling of being responsible for this tiny human... it all just feels so overwhelming. And sometimes, when I'm feeling really down, I'll just start crying. I'll be sitting there, holding my baby, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me.

It's not all the time, though. Some days are better than others. When my baby smiles at me, or laughs, or does something new, it's like all the sadness just melts away. But on the hard days, when everything feels like too much, I'll just feel sad. I'll feel like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not good enough, or that I'm just not cut out for this whole mom thing.

My husband tries to be supportive, and he'll tell me that I'm doing a great job, and that it's okay to feel sad sometimes. But it's hard to shake off the feeling that I'm somehow failing, or that I'm not living up to some kind of expectation. I guess that's just part of being a new mom, though. It's a lot of pressure, and it's okay to not be okay all the time.

Sometimes, when I'm feeling really sad, I'll just talk to my husband about it. I'll tell him how I'm feeling, and he'll listen, and he'll remind me that it's okay to feel that way. And sometimes, just talking about it makes me feel a little better. But other times, it's like the sadness just lingers, and I'll feel it for days. It's like, I know I'm not alone, but it's hard to remember that when I'm feeling really down.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I'd say that's been true for me, unfortunately. As a new mom, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and emotional, and I've found myself crying a lot more often than I used to. It's like, I'll be doing something, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness or frustration, and I'll start crying.

Sometimes it's because I'm feeling overwhelmed by all the responsibilities of taking care of a new baby. Other times, it's because I'm feeling anxious or worried about something. And sometimes, it's just because I'm feeling really tired and exhausted, and I just can't seem to catch a break.

I've been trying to talk to my husband about it, and he's been really supportive. He'll listen to me and try to help me figure out what's going on, and he'll remind me that it's okay to feel overwhelmed. But even with his support, it's hard not to feel like I'm just losing it sometimes.

The crying is just so frustrating, because I feel like I'm not in control of my emotions. I'll be sitting there, trying to feed my baby or change her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's like, I'm not even sure what's triggering it, or how to make it stop. And then, of course, my baby will start crying too, because she can sense that I'm upset, and it's just this whole big cycle of tears and frustration.

It's not all the time, though. Some days are better than others, and I'll go for hours without crying. But on the days when I do cry, it's like, I'll cry for hours. I'll just feel so overwhelmed and emotional, and I won't be able to stop.

I guess it's just part of being a new mom, though. I've heard that it's normal to feel emotional and overwhelmed after having a baby, and that it's okay to cry sometimes. But it's hard to remember that when I'm in the midst of it all, and I'm just feeling like I'm losing my mind.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

* Persistent sadness and crying spells

This screening summary highlights the patient's emotional and behavioral concerns, which may indicate a need for further evaluation and support to address potential postpartum depression and anxiety.
